title: Verdt å eller lønne seg — worth and practical benefit
goal: Choose general worth versus practical payoff.

objectives.statement: Choose general worth versus practical payoff.

spans.value: Jonas and Selma are planning a weekend trip from Oslo to Røros. The train is comfortable but expensive, while the bus is cheaper and takes longer. Selma also wants to visit a small museum outside the town centre.
Togbillettene er ganske dyre. Tror du det er verdt å ta toget?

blocks.translation: The train tickets are quite expensive. Do you think it is worth taking the train?

spans.value: Ja, kanskje. Utsikten er fin, og vi kan slappe av underveis.

blocks.translation: Yes, perhaps. The view is beautiful, and we can relax along the way.

spans.value: Men det lønner seg å bestille i dag. Prisene blir sikkert høyere i morgen.

blocks.translation: But it pays to book today. The prices will probably be higher tomorrow.

spans.value: Enig. Hva med museet på søndag? Det ligger et stykke utenfor sentrum.

blocks.translation: Agreed. What about the museum on Sunday? It is some distance outside the town centre.

spans.value: Jeg har hørt at det er lite, men veldig interessant. Det er visst verdt å besøke.

blocks.translation: I have heard that it is small but very interesting. Apparently, it is worth visiting.

spans.value: Da kan det lønne seg å kjøpe et helgekort til bussen. Vi skal jo reise flere ganger.

blocks.translation: Then it may pay to buy a weekend bus pass. We are going to travel several times, after all.

spans.value: Two expressions do similar work here, but they point to different kinds of value:

items.value: gives a general evaluation: an experience, action, or thing deserves the time, effort, attention, or cost.
emphasizes a practical payoff: an action produces an advantage, saves something, or gives a useful result.

spans.value: Jonas and Selma think the train and museum may be good experiences. They also calculate when to book and which ticket will give them a practical advantage.
Use
verdt å + infinitive
when you evaluate whether doing something is worthwhile in a broad sense.

no.value: Det er verdt å ta toget.

en.value: It is worth taking the train.

no.value: Museet er verdt å besøke.

en.value: The museum is worth visiting.

no.value: Denne boka er verdt å lese.

en.value: This book is worth reading.

no.value: Det er verdt å vente litt.

en.value: It is worth waiting a little.

spans.value: The value may come from enjoyment, quality, interest, importance, or a meaningful experience. It does not have to involve a measurable benefit.
Compare two common patterns:

no.value: Det er verdt å se utstillingen.

en.value: It is worth seeing the exhibition.

no.value: Utstillingen er verdt å se.

en.value: The exhibition is worth seeing.

spans.value: In the first pattern,
det
introduces an evaluation of an action. In the second, the thing being evaluated comes first. Both patterns use
å
before the infinitive.
You can also make the evaluation negative:

no.value: Det er ikke verdt å krangle om det.

en.value: It is not worth arguing about it.

no.value: Filmen er ikke verdt å se.

en.value: The film is not worth seeing.

spans.value: Here, the speaker judges that the action does not deserve the required time, effort, or attention.
Checkpoint: identify broad evaluations
Read several short statements about travel, books, films, events, and everyday decisions. Mark the statements that evaluate general quality, interest, or experience rather than a concrete advantage.
This activity belongs here because the first step is recognizing the meaning of
verdt å
before producing it. A successful response would consistently identify evaluations such as whether a museum deserves a visit or whether a film deserves the viewer’s time.
Use
lønne seg
when an action gives a practical benefit. The benefit is often financial, but it may also involve saving time, avoiding difficulty, or getting a better result.

no.value: Det lønner seg å bestille tidlig.

en.value: It pays to book early.

no.value: Det lønner seg å sammenligne prisene.

en.value: It pays to compare the prices.

no.value: Det lønner seg å ta med matpakke.

en.value: It is worthwhile to bring a packed lunch.

no.value: Det lønner seg å spørre før du kjøper billetten.

en.value: It pays to ask before you buy the ticket.

spans.value: The Norwegian expression contains the reflexive pronoun
seg
. Keep the whole expression together:
lønne seg
A very common frame is:

no.value: Det lønner seg å + infinitive.

en.value: It pays to + infinitive.

spans.value: You can add
kan
when the benefit depends on the situation:

no.value: Det kan lønne seg å kjøpe et helgekort.

en.value: It may pay to buy a weekend pass.

no.value: Det kan lønne seg å vente på et bedre tilbud.

en.value: It may be worthwhile to wait for a better offer.

spans.value: The negative form means that an action does not provide enough practical benefit:

no.value: Det lønner seg ikke å ta taxi når bussen går hvert tiende minutt.

en.value: It does not pay to take a taxi when the bus runs every ten minutes.

no.value: Det lønner seg ikke å kjøpe enkeltbilletter hvis du skal reise mye.

en.value: It does not pay to buy single tickets if you are going to travel a lot.

spans.value: Checkpoint: find the practical advantage
For each short situation, state what would be gained or saved by the suggested action. Use contexts such as booking early, comparing prices, taking a direct bus, or buying several items together.

This activity makes the practical meaning explicit. A successful response would identify a concrete payoff—money saved, less time used, fewer problems, or a better result—rather than merely saying that the action is pleasant or interesting.
Both expressions can correspond to English phrases such as
worth it
worthwhile
, or
it pays to
. The Norwegian choice depends on the speaker’s intended reason.
Experience versus saving money

no.value: Det er verdt å ta toget fordi utsikten er fantastisk.

en.value: It is worth taking the train because the view is fantastic.

no.value: Det lønner seg å ta toget fordi barn reiser gratis i helgene.

en.value: It pays to take the train because children travel free at weekends.

spans.value: The action is the same, but the reason changes. A beautiful view supports a broad evaluation with
verdt å
. Free travel creates a practical benefit, so
lønner seg
is more natural.
Quality versus useful result

no.value: Kurset er verdt å ta fordi læreren er svært dyktig.

en.value: The course is worth taking because the teacher is highly skilled.

no.value: Det lønner seg å ta kurset før du søker på jobben.

en.value: It pays to take the course before you apply for the job.

spans.value: The first sentence evaluates the course’s quality. The second presents the course as a useful step toward a result.
Interest versus efficiency

no.value: Det er verdt å gå gjennom gamlebyen.

en.value: It is worth walking through the old town.

no.value: Det lønner seg å gå gjennom gamlebyen når hovedveien er stengt.

en.value: It pays to walk through the old town when the main road is closed.

spans.value: In the first sentence, the walk is worth experiencing. In the second, the route solves a practical problem.
Personal significance versus calculation

no.value: Det er verdt å reise langt for å møte gamle venner.

en.value: It is worth travelling a long way to meet old friends.

no.value: Det lønner seg å kjøpe billettene sammen.

en.value: It pays to buy the tickets together.

spans.value: Meeting friends has personal value. Buying tickets together offers a calculable advantage.
Sometimes both forms are grammatically possible, but they frame the action differently.

no.value: Det er verdt å lære noen norske uttrykk før reisen.

en.value: It is worth learning some Norwegian expressions before the trip.

spans.value: This suggests that learning the expressions is valuable or rewarding in general.

no.value: Det lønner seg å lære noen norske uttrykk før reisen.

en.value: It pays to learn some Norwegian expressions before the trip.

spans.value: This emphasizes a practical result: communication may become easier, and the traveller may avoid misunderstandings.
Another pair:

no.value: Det er verdt å stå opp tidlig for å se soloppgangen.

en.value: It is worth getting up early to see the sunrise.

spans.value: The experience deserves the effort.

no.value: Det lønner seg å stå opp tidlig hvis du vil unngå kø.

en.value: It pays to get up early if you want to avoid the queue.

spans.value: Getting up early produces a concrete advantage.
The distinction is therefore not always about the action itself. It is about how the speaker presents the action.
Checkpoint: choose according to the reason

Complete paired sentences in which the action remains the same but the reason changes. One reason should concern quality, interest, enjoyment, or personal importance; the other should concern cost, time, convenience, or results.
This controlled contrast belongs here because it prevents learners from choosing only from the verb or topic. A successful response would use
verdt å
and
lønne seg
according to the stated reason.
These frames cover many everyday situations.
Evaluating an experience or thing

no.value: Det er verdt å prøve.

en.value: It is worth trying.

no.value: Stedet er verdt å besøke.

en.value: The place is worth visiting.

no.value: Boka er ikke verdt å kjøpe.

en.value: The book is not worth buying.

no.value: Er det verdt å vente?

en.value: Is it worth waiting?

spans.value: Recommending a practical action

no.value: Det lønner seg å planlegge på forhånd.

en.value: It pays to plan in advance.

no.value: Det kan lønne seg å ringe først.

en.value: It may pay to call first.

no.value: Det lønner seg ikke å kjøpe den dyreste modellen.

en.value: It does not pay to buy the most expensive model.

no.value: Lønner det seg å bestille på nettet?

en.value: Does it pay to book online?

spans.value: Notice the question forms:

no.value: Er det verdt å ta en omvei?

en.value: Is it worth taking a detour?

no.value: Lønner det seg å ta en omvei?

en.value: Does it pay to take a detour?

spans.value: The first asks whether the detour deserves the effort, perhaps because the route is beautiful. The second asks whether the detour brings a practical advantage, perhaps because it avoids traffic.
Checkpoint: build complete frames
Given brief prompts containing an action and a reason, write complete sentences with either
det er verdt å
or
det lønner seg å
. Include affirmative, negative, and question forms.
This activity moves from recognition to controlled production. A successful response would preserve the complete expression, place
å
before the infinitive, and choose the frame that matches the kind of value.
Do not omit å after verdt
Incorrect:

no.value: ✗ Det er verdt besøke museet.

en.value: ✗ It is worth visit the museum.

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Det er verdt å besøke museet.

en.value: It is worth visiting the museum.

spans.value: The fixed frame is
verdt å + infinitive
Do not omit seg from lønne seg
Incorrect:

no.value: ✗ Det lønner å bestille tidlig.

en.value: ✗ It pays to book early.

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Det lønner seg å bestille tidlig.

en.value: It pays to book early.

spans.value: The reflexive pronoun is part of the expression.
Do not use lønne seg only for direct profit
Lønne seg
often concerns money, but its practical meaning is wider.

no.value: Det lønner seg å sjekke værmeldingen før turen.

en.value: It pays to check the weather forecast before the trip.

spans.value: The speaker may not earn money. The payoff is better preparation and fewer problems.

no.value: Det lønner seg å skrive ned adressen.

en.value: It pays to write down the address.

spans.value: The practical benefit is avoiding confusion later.
Do not treat the expressions as automatic synonyms

no.value: Konserten var fantastisk. Det var verdt å vente.

en.value: The concert was fantastic. It was worth waiting.

no.value: Vi fikk billetter til halv pris. Det lønte seg å vente.

en.value: We got tickets at half price. It paid to wait.

spans.value: The concert made the wait worthwhile as an experience.
The wait produced a concrete benefit.
The surrounding information determines the intended meaning.
Checkpoint: repair meaning and form
Revise short sentences containing either a missing element or an expression that conflicts with the reason given. Keep the original situation but make the recommendation natural.
This activity combines form and meaning after both have been introduced. A successful response would restore
å
or
seg
where necessary and distinguish general worth from practical payoff.
Later that evening, Jonas checks the transport website.
Jeg fant et billigere tog. Det går klokka seks om morgenen.

blocks.translation: I found a cheaper train. It leaves at six in the morning.

spans.value: Så tidlig? Lønner det seg virkelig?

blocks.translation: That early? Does it really pay off?

spans.value: Vi sparer nesten åtte hundre kroner, og vi får hele ettermiddagen i Røros.

blocks.translation: We save almost eight hundred kroner, and we get the whole afternoon in Røros.

spans.value: Da lønner det seg nok å stå opp tidlig.

blocks.translation: Then it probably pays to get up early.

spans.value: Jeg fant også en guidet tur i en gammel gruve. Den er litt dyr.

blocks.translation: I also found a guided tour in an old mine. It is a little expensive.

spans.value: Søsteren min tok den turen i fjor. Hun sa at den absolutt var verdt å ta.

blocks.translation: My sister took that tour last year. She said that it was definitely worth taking.

spans.value: Greit. Vi sparer penger på toget, så det er verdt å bruke litt mer på gruveturen.

blocks.translation: All right. We will save money on the train, so it is worth spending a little more on the mine tour.

spans.value: The dialogue now contains both sides of the distinction. Getting up early has a practical payoff: they save money and gain time. The mine tour is evaluated as a worthwhile experience despite its price.

Continue Jonas and Selma’s planning in writing. Respond to short developments such as a discount on advance tickets, an excellent but distant restaurant, a slow route with beautiful scenery, or a travel card that covers several journeys. Use one target expression in each response and include a brief reason.
This activity returns to the chapter’s main context while introducing new decisions. A successful response would connect enjoyable or meaningful experiences with
verdt å
, and measurable advantages with
lønne seg
Without looking back, write one sentence recommending an experience with
verdt å
, one sentence recommending a practical action with
lønne seg
, and one question that could take either expression depending on the reason. Add a short reason to each sentence so the intended distinction is clear.

prompt.value: Sort each Norwegian statement into General worth or Practical payoff. Choose the bucket that matches the meaning of the statement.

explanation.value: Verdt å gives a broad evaluation of worth; lønne seg describes a practical payoff for the subject.

items.text: Det lønner seg å bestille tidlig.
Filmen er ikke verdt å se.
Det lønner seg å sammenligne prisene.
Det er verdt å stå opp tidlig for å se soloppgangen.
Det lønner seg å skrive ned adressen.

prompt.value: For each situation, write one short sentence in Norwegian stating the concrete practical advantage. Do not give only a general evaluation such as saying that the action is pleasant or interesting. 1. Book train tickets several weeks before departure instead of at the last minute. 2. Compare prices at several shops before buying the same item. 3. Take a direct bus instead of a route with changes. 4. Buy several items together when a shop offers a lower total price for the group.

payload.judge_prompt: Check each sentence against its situation and report evidence for the criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants when they clearly name a concrete benefit or saving.

criteria.instruction: For all four situations, states a concrete benefit or saving such as money, time, fewer problems, or a better result rather than only pleasure or interest.

prompt.value: Choose the pair that completes the two reasons in order. The action is taking a detour. Reason one is broad: the view is beautiful, so the experience deserves the effort. Reason two is practical: the detour helps avoid traffic.

options.text: Det lønner seg å ta en omvei fordi utsikten er vakker. Det er verdt å ta en omvei fordi du unngår kø.
options.why: The expressions are reversed for the stated broad and practical reasons.

options.text: Det er verdt å ta en omvei fordi utsikten er vakker. Det lønner seg å ta en omvei fordi du unngår kø.
options.why: The first sentence presents a beautiful view as general worth; the second presents avoiding traffic as practical payoff.

stem.value: Choose the Norwegian pair that matches the two reasons.

prompt.value: Build three complete Norwegian sentences from the supplied tokens in this order. Use every token exactly once. Sentence one is an affirmative general evaluation of seeing the exhibition. Sentence two is a negative practical recommendation about taking a taxi when the bus runs every ten minutes. Sentence three is a question about whether taking a detour is broadly worthwhile.
Select the token where the practical-payoff expression is incomplete. The feedback gives the complete form.

payload.feedback: The practical-payoff expression is lønne seg. Add seg after lønner and before å; the repaired sentence is Det lønner seg å bestille tidlig.

prompt.value: Write four short Norwegian recommendations, one for each development. Use one target expression in each response and include a brief reason. 1. Advance tickets are discounted when bought early. 2. The restaurant is excellent but far away. 3. The slower route has beautiful scenery. 4. A travel card covers several journeys.

payload.judge_prompt: Check each recommendation against its development and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants with the required target expression and a clear reason.

criteria.instruction: Uses verdt å for the excellent distant restaurant and the scenic slow route, with a reason showing quality or experience.
Uses lønner seg for the discounted advance tickets and the travel card, with a reason showing a measurable advantage.

prompt.value: Write two Norwegian sentences about the same action: getting up early. In the first sentence, the reason is that the roads are quieter and traffic is easier; use the practical-payoff expression. In the second sentence, the reason is that the sunrise over the fjord is beautiful; use the general-worth expression. Keep the action constant and include the reason in each sentence.

payload.judge_prompt: Check both sentences for the same action, the requested reason, and the matching target expression. Report evidence for each criterion and accept natural Bokmål variants.

criteria.instruction: Keeps getting up early as the same action in both sentences.
Uses lønner seg for the practical traffic reason and verdt å for the broad sunrise experience.

prompt.value: Without looking back, write in Norwegian. Write one sentence recommending an experience with verdt å and a short general-worth reason. Write one sentence recommending a practical action with lønner seg and a short concrete-benefit reason. Finally, write one question about the same action in two versions: use verdt å with a broad reason and lønner seg with a practical reason. Add a short reason to each sentence.

payload.judge_prompt: Check all recommendations and both versions of the question against the task. Report evidence for each criterion and accept natural Bokmål variants that keep the intended distinction clear.

criteria.instruction: The experience recommendation uses verdt å and gives a short general-worth reason.
The practical-action recommendation uses lønner seg and gives a short concrete-benefit reason.
The same action appears in both question versions, with verdt å for the broad reason and lønner seg for the practical reason.
Each sentence includes a short reason that makes its intended framing clear.
